(c) In order to prove the adverse possession, there should be specific pleadings as about the date of occupation and the plaintiff has to prove that her position is ("Nec vi, Nec clam, Nec precario").
But there is no evidence to prove that the plaintiff and her predecessors have been in continuous and uninterrupted possession of the property within the knowledge of one and all to attract the conditions for adverse possession.
The plaintiff obtained the Settlement Deed from her father in respect of the property and thereby, she is the owner of the property through a Settlement https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 04/11/2025 09:30:40 pm ) and Deed.
To claim adverse possession, the plaintiff ought to have admitted the title of the property in favour of the defendant, but during the cross-examination, D.W.1 denied the title of the defendant.
Moreover, the plaintiff's father filed Suits against third parties and the defendant only for the relief of permanent injunction.
The Suit against the defendant was filed in the year 1993 alleging that they tried to dispossess the plaintiff's father from the Suit property.
Even though the dispute arose in the year 1993 itself, the plaintiff has not filed any Suit against the defendant in respect of the title of the property.
(d) Though the plaintiff pleaded that her father acquired the property in the year 1957, after obtaining Settlement Deed in her favour, she is entitled to the property only through the Settlement Deed, but not produced any documents to prove her continuous and uninterrupted possession.
Therefore, in order to prove the said claim there are no sufficient pleadings and the evidence adduced by the plaintiff.
Per contra, her husband was examined as P.W.1.
Though the husband is the competent witness to the Suit on behalf of P.W.1, who is his wife, as per Section 120 of the Evidence Act, 1872,
the personal knowledge of the plaintiff in respect of the adverse possession cannot be witnessed by P.W.1.
(e) It is well-settled law that mere long possession cannot create any adverse possession.
The possession must be ("Nec vi, Nec clam, Nec precario").
In order to prove the said possession for more than 30 years, no sufficient evidence is produced by the plaintiff.
Therefore, the plaintiff has failed to prove the adverse possession.
The subject property, along with the adjacent property,
was allotted for public purpose and the adjacent land was leased out by the defendant to one Trust for running School.
Moreover, the conduct of the parties by not taking steps with regard to the allotment of alternative land clearly establishes that the plaintiff is making an attempt to get the property as if her land was acquired by the Government, having failed to prove the said acquisition, which is base for the claim of the plaintiff and without producing documents for the long and uninterrupted possession, she is not entitled to claim adverse possession.
Further, it is clear that a Court should necessarily seek an answer to whether the plaintiff has produced title deeds tracing the title for a period of more than thirty years or whether the plaintiff has established his adverse possession to the knowledge of the Government for a period of more than thirty (30) years so as to convert his possession into title and mere temporary use or occupation without the animus to claim ownership or mere use at sufferance will not be sufficient to create any right adverse to the Government.
Therefore, she is not entitled to relief of adverse possession as against the defendant.
Therefore, the plaintiff would not be entitled to a permanent injunction in respect of the Suit property.
